s1.syndrome_frame: Acute episodic chest pain with exertion
salient_findings: Substernal chest pain triggered by running more than 2 miles
ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test
Severe ischemia in the distribution of the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries on PET-MPI
key_facts: Substernal chest pain lasting less than 5 minutes
Chest pain occurs with running more than 2 miles
Hypertension controlled with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide
No family history of premature coronary artery disease
No chest pain during exercise treadmill test
ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute episodic chest pain with exertion
salient_findings: Substernal chest pain triggered by running more than 2 miles
ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test
Severe ischemia in the distribution of the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries on PET-MPI
key_facts: Substernal chest pain lasting less than 5 minutes

Hypertension controlled with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide
No family history of premature coronary artery disease
No chest pain during exercise treadmill test
ST depressions during recovery phase of exercise treadmill test

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of substernal chest pain with exertion, high LDL levels, and the results of the exercise treadmill test, CCTA, PET-MPI, and coronary angiogram all support the diagnosis of coronary artery disease, particularly with the demonstration of 3-vessel involvement and severe ischemia in the distribution of the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries.

rejected.label: dyslipidemia
rejected.why: While the patient has high LDL levels, dyslipidemia is a risk factor for coronary artery disease but does not directly explain the chest pain and ischemia findings.

rejected.label: cardiovascular
rejected.why: This is too broad and does not specifically address the patient's symptoms and test results.

rejected.label: acute coronary syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's chest pain is brief and occurs with exertion, and there is no mention of acute symptoms like persistent chest pain or ECG changes during pain, which are typical of acute coronary syndrome.

rejected.label: myocardial ischemia
rejected.why: While the patient does have myocardial ischemia as evidenced by the PET-MPI and stress test results, coronary artery disease is the underlying cause of the ischemia and better explains the overall clinical picture.
